The image displays a frontal view of the chest, showing both lungs, the heart, clavicles, and ribs in a single plane. This orientation corresponds to the coronal anatomical plane (frontal plane), which divides the body into anterior and posterior sections. In radiography, a standard PA or AP chest X-ray is considered a projection onto the coronal plane. Therefore, it represents a coronal section/view.

{"answer":"B. yes","reason":"The image is a frontal chest radiograph displaying anatomy in the coronal plane."}
